info.title: Inlet API
info.description:
Inlet separates form definition from form rendering and response storage. Your
application fetches a published form definition, renders it however it likes, and
posts the answers back in one call.

## Collecting feedback in four calls

```bash
BASE=http://192.168.0.19:3000
KEY=ipk_your_publishable_client_key
DB=fdb_your_feedback_database_id

# 1. Read the published form
curl -s "$BASE/v1/feedback-databases/$DB/form" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"

# 2. Open a submission intent
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/v1/feedback-databases/$DB/submission-intents" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"

# 3. Optionally attach a screenshot
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/v1/feedback-databases/$DB/submission-intents/$INTENT/attachments" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Inlet-Intent-Token: $TOKEN" \
  -F questionId=el_xxxxxxxxxxxx -F file=@screenshot.png

# 4. Submit everything at once
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/v1/feedback-databases/$DB/submission-intents/$INTENT/submit" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Inlet-Intent-Token: $TOKEN" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"formVersion":1,"answers":{"el_xxxxxxxxxxxx":{"value":"It works"}}}'
```

## Two kinds of key

A **publishable client key** (`ipk_…`) is safe to embed in a browser or mobile
app. It authorizes only the four calls above.

A **secret server key** (`isk_…`) carries project Admin authority: it can read
and export submissions, manage forms, and delete data within its own project.
Keep it on a server. It is shown once, when you create it.

Send either as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. The management interface uses a
session cookie instead, obtained from `POST /v1/auth/sign-in`.

## Answers

Answers are keyed by stable question ID. The shape follows the question type in
the pinned form version, so you never repeat the type:

| Question type | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| single-select choice | `{"optionId": "op_…"}` |
| multi-select choice | `{"optionIds": ["op_…", "op_…"]}` |
| single- or multi-line text | `{"value": "…"}` |
| email | `{"value": "someone@example.com"}` |
| screenshot upload | `{"attachmentIds": ["att_…"]}` |

Omit a question entirely to leave an optional question unanswered. An empty
string never satisfies a required question.

## Retrying safely

Every submission starts with a server-issued intent, which makes retries safe.
Repeating a finalization with the same payload returns the original result;
repeating it with a different payload is a conflict and stores nothing; and a
validation failure leaves the intent usable so you can correct and resend.

## Limits

- `clientContext`: 16384 bytes serialized as UTF-8.
- Screenshots: JPEG, PNG or WebP, 2 MB and 25 megapixels per file, 5 per submission, 10 uploads per intent. Animated images are rejected and every accepted image is re-encoded to WebP.
- Security rate limits apply to sign-in, intent creation, uploads and
  finalization. They are not configurable.

## Errors

Every failure returns `{"error":{"code","message","details?"}}`. The `code` is
stable and safe to branch on; `details` carries `questionId` for answer problems
and `path` for request-shape problems.

projectKey.description: A project credential: a publishable client key (`ipk_…`) for the feedback flow, or a secret server key (`isk_…`) for everything in its project.

session.name: inlet_session
session.description: The management session cookie set by POST /v1/auth/sign-in.

details.description: Field- or question-level detail, when relevant.

id.description: The stable public identifier used by client applications (FR-021).

activeFormVersion.description: Null when the form is unpublished.

problems.description: Why this draft cannot be published yet. Empty when it is publishable.

key.description: The publishable key value. Null for secret keys.

token.description: Single-use bearer token for uploads and finalization.

formVersion.description: The pinned version. Finalization must name this value.

status.description: "duplicate" means this intent had already been finalized with this payload.

attachmentId.description: Reference this ID in the submission payload.

scanStatus.description: The malware scan outcome. "skipped" when no scanner is configured, "error" when one was configured but unreachable and the deployment accepts uploads anyway. An infected file is refused and never reaches this response.

url.description: Stable authenticated URL. Every request is authorized (FR-069).

formDefinition.description: The definition this submission was made against, for label-accurate display (FR-065).

role.description: The role assigned at this scope.

effectiveRole.description: The role that actually applies, after the override rules of FR-071.

inherited.description: True when the role comes from the project rather than this feedback database.

scopeName.description: The name of what the invitation grants access to.

requiresAccount.description: False when the caller is already signed in, so no password is needed.

post.summary: Sign in with email and password
post.description: Starts a management session. The session is an HTTP-only cookie; API clients use a project key instead.

get.summary: List the projects you can access

post.description: The creating user becomes the project’s first Admin (FR-010).

delete.description: Deletes its feedback databases, forms, submissions, attachments, memberships and credentials (FR-026). Screenshot objects are purged asynchronously (FR-027).

purgedKeys.description: Screenshot objects queued for asynchronous purge (FR-027).

get.summary: List the feedback databases of a project

post.description: Creates the one logical form of this database, as an empty draft.

get.description: Secret server keys are listed without their value (FR-084).

post.summary: Create a publishable client key or a secret server key
post.description: The response is the only time a secret server key’s value is returned (FR-084).

key.description: The publishable key value. Null for secret keys.

secret.description: The full key. A secret server key is shown here once and never again (FR-084).

post.description: Replaces the value in place, keeping the ID and label. The previous value stops working immediately.

key.description: The publishable key value. Null for secret keys.

secret.description: The full key. A secret server key is shown here once and never again (FR-084).

post.description: Every subsequent request authenticated with it is refused.

delete.description: Deletes its form versions, submissions, answers, attachments, pending uploads and memberships (FR-024). Records go immediately; screenshot objects are purged asynchronously (FR-027).

purgedKeys.description: Screenshot objects queued for asynchronous purge (FR-027).

get.summary: What deleting this feedback database would destroy
get.description: Powers the warning required before destructive deletion (FR-025), including the notice that exports contain no screenshot files.
Reopening the builder restores this draft. `problems` lists why it cannot be published yet (FR-042).

put.description: Replaces the draft definition and increments its revision. Concurrent saves are last-write-wins (FR-042A).

get.summary: List published form versions, newest first

post.summary: Publish the draft as a new immutable version
post.description: Creates a version from the current draft and makes it active. Existing submission intents keep their pinned version (FR-042G).

expectedRevision.description: Reject the publish if the draft has moved past this revision (FR-042C).

post.description: Blocks client retrieval and new submission intents. Versions and historical submissions are untouched, and issued intents still finalize (FR-042F, FR-042G).

version.description: Defaults to the most recent inactive version.

get.summary: Retrieve the active published form definition
get.description: Elements are returned in authored order. Screenshot questions carry the platform’s accepted media types and per-file size limit (FR-046).

post.description: Returns a single-use token scoped to one feedback database and pinned to one published form version.

formVersion.description: The version the client rendered. Defaults to the active version.

post.summary: Upload a screenshot under a submission intent
post.description: Multipart form data with a `questionId` field and a `file` part. The image is validated by content, re-encoded to WebP, and returned as an attachment ID to reference at finalization.

parameters.name: x-inlet-intent-token
parameters.description: The token returned when the submission intent was created.

delete.summary: Discard a pending screenshot before submitting
delete.description: Optional. Not referencing an upload at finalization has the same effect; this releases the bytes immediately (FR-047).

parameters.name: x-inlet-intent-token
parameters.description: The token returned when the submission intent was created.

formVersion.description: Must equal the version pinned on the intent (FR-094).

clientContext.description: Arbitrary JSON kept as supplied, at most 16384 bytes as UTF-8.

parameters.name: x-inlet-intent-token
parameters.description: The token returned when the submission intent was created.

get.summary: Export submissions as JSON or CSV
get.description: Raw answers including collected email addresses, the form version, timestamp, observed IP and clientContext. Screenshots appear as stable authenticated URLs; the files are not bundled (FR-112).
Includes the definition of the form version this submission was made against, so answers can be shown with the labels the respondent saw (FR-065).

delete.summary: Permanently delete one submission and its screenshots
delete.description: Re-finalizing the submission’s intent afterwards returns 410 `submission_deleted` and exposes no answers (FR-092G).

purgedKeys.description: Screenshot objects queued for asynchronous purge (FR-027).

get.description: Requires a management session or a secret server key with at least Viewer access to the attachment’s feedback database.

get.summary: List the people with access to a project

patch.description: Downgrading the last Admin is rejected with 409 `last_admin_removal` (FR-014). Promoting someone to Admin clears any feedback-database override, which could only narrow access an Admin must keep (FR-071A).

delete.description: Removing the last Admin is rejected (FR-014). Their feedback-database assignments inside the project go with them.

get.summary: List who can reach one feedback database
get.description: Includes people who reach it through the project and people with an assignment on it, with the effective role of FR-071 resolved for each.

put.summary: Assign a role on one feedback database
put.description: Overrides the project role for this database only (FR-071). Refused for a project Admin, whose access cannot be narrowed (FR-071A).

delete.description: The person keeps whatever their project role gives them. This removes the override, not their access.

post.description: Returns a single-use link that expires. Send it through your own channel; Inlet sends no email. The link is shown once.

scopeName.description: The name of what the invitation grants access to.

token.description: The single-use token. Returned once, at creation.

url.description: The link to send. Built from INLET_PUBLIC_URL.

post.summary: Invite someone to one feedback database
post.description: The role applies to this feedback database only. Use a project invitation to grant access across a whole project.

scopeName.description: The name of what the invitation grants access to.

token.description: The single-use token. Returned once, at creation.

url.description: The link to send. Built from INLET_PUBLIC_URL.

get.description: Public, so someone can see what they are accepting before they accept it. Reveals only the role and the scope’s name.

post.description:
Grants exactly the role and scope recorded on the invitation, whatever address the redeemer uses (FR-007), and consumes it.

Signed in already: send no body and the invitation attaches to that account.
No account yet: send an email and a password, and the account is created.

A second use, an expiry or a revocation all fail, each with its own code.
